headline: Zone change hearings for 95 Vernon St., 25 West Chester St., 128 Providence St., and 321 Greenwood St.; also a proposed change to inclusionary zoning payments.
summary: The committee will hold zone change hearings on four properties. It will also discuss raising the Payment in Lieu of constructing affordable housing from 3 to 5 percent of total construction value.
items: Zone change hearing on a petition by George Markopoulos for 95 Vernon Street LLC to establish the Adaptive Re-use Overlay District (AROD) at 95 Vernon St.
Zone change hearing on a petition by Timothy J. McMahon of Catholic Charities of the Diocese of Worcester to establish the AROD at 25 West Chester St.
Zone change hearing on a City Manager communication to extend the RG-5 (Residence, General) district and AROD to 128 Providence St.

Zone change hearing on a petition by George Markopoulos for 321 Greenwood Street LLC to change part of 321 Green Wood St. (MBL: 29-043-00003) from Manufacturing, Limited (ML-0.5) to Business, Limited (BL-1.0)
Report on a City Manager communication recommending adoption of a Zoning Ordinance amendment related to driveways, pavement, and permits (held in committee June 25, 2026)

Order of Councilor Robert A. Bilotta to hold a public discussion on amending Section 5 of the Inclusionary Zoning Ordinance to raise the Payment in Lieu of affordable housing from 3 percent to 5 percent of total construction value of all building permits, including trade permits
location: Esther Howland (South) Chamber, City Hall, 455 Main Street, Worcester, Massachusetts

Important Notice: Residents are advised of an ongoing scam involving the impersonation 
of city officials and departments. Scammers are fraudulently requesting payments be 
made for planning and zoning permits, as well as City Council petitions. All official 
emails regarding your petition will come exclusively from an @worcesterma.gov email 
address (such as clerk @worcesterma.gov), or via physical mail on the City of 
Worcester’s official letterhead. Any legitimate hearing letter will always include your 
specific application details, along with the scheduled hearing date, time, and location . 
The City of Worcester will never request payments via wire transfer.
